headline: Australia's hotels industry released a satirical video, which The Mercury calls an AI video, picturing empty cafes and a $47 apple if migrant workers are cut.
score_reason: Light satirical ad in a live political debate; AI use is only asserted in the Mercury headline.
importance_line: It adds an industry voice to Australia's argument over immigration cuts; whether the ad was made with AI is stated only in The Mercury's headline.
source: AI News Desk, from The Mercury and 7NEWS
summary: 7NEWS reports that the Australian Hotels Association released a humorous advertisement showing cafes, aged care and supermarkets suffering if Labor, the Coalition and One Nation cut migrant labour, and The Mercury headlines it as a viral AI video from Hospitality Tasmania. Association chief executive Stephen Ferguson says no party is discussing the knock-on effects, and the 7NEWS report does not say how the video was made.
notes: Mercury original blocked; text read from 7NEWS (https://7news.com.au/news/aussie-hotel-association-makes-pro-migration-move-with-new-advertisment-c-23015557). AI claim unverified; link of Hospitality Tasmania to the AHA assumed, not confirmed.
